newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS -- California diesel falls amid ample supplies.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS -- California diesel falls amid ample supplies.

text.p: Plentiful diesel supplies in the Los Angeles area have pushed prices at distribution terminals down and forced local refiners to cut wholesale prices eight percent in the last week, traders said Tuesday.

They said Atlantic Richfield Co, a top marketer in California, led the drive to discount diesel amid growing supplies in the region. ARCO is known to sell more aggressively when it is "long" a given product.
Wholesale prices for California Air Resource Board (CARB) number two diesel fuel were pegged 65.50 cents a gallon early Tuesday, down six cents from a week earlier.
Wholesale prices are set at refinery pipelines, while values at distribution terminals, or "racks," are set at the end of the pipeline and include storage and handling costs.
"The racks all got cut again last night...down over a penny. That's what's applying pressure," said a products broker based in California.
Rack prices for CARB diesel in Los Angeles averaged 68 cents early Tuesday, falling five cents a gallon since April 22, according to traders and industry observers.
Some traders also speculated ARCO may be selling a bit harder before it starts unspecified maintencance activity at its Carson refinery in the Los Angeles area in the hopes of pushing prices down.
An ARCO trader declined comment on the company's pricing strategies, but said rack prices are influenced by competition among gasoline retailers.
Asked if problems with a processing unit has caused ARCO's diesel supplies to back up and contributed to the ample supply situation, the ARCO trader said: "We have no operational problems."
Some traders speculated a fluid catalytic cracking unit at the Carson plant that uses diesel as a feedstock might be hobbled.

West Coast distillate inventories, which include diesel, were about unchanged last week from prior week levels -- about 1.1 million barrels over a year ago, according to data released by the American Petroleum Institute Tuesday.
